alpha.hint: Sets the source to the alpha repository and the channel to Beta.
alpha.warningBody: Alpha versions are test builds with hotfixes. Their images are not signed, not tested extensively and meant for test installations only, never for production data. Anyone with write access to the alpha repository can deliver code that runs with the database and the master key.
alpha.setup: Once on the server: in .env set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY and RESTOW_UPDATER_WEB_IMAGE_REPOSITORY to the alpha images (…/restow-alpha and …/restow-alpha-web) and RESTOW_UPDATER_VERIFY_SIGNATURES=false, then recreate the updater. After that, alpha updates run from this page.

updater.title: Installing updates

description.unavailable: Update by hand, or start the optional updater to install updates from this page.
description.ready: Announce an update here. The updater takes a database backup first and rolls back if the new version does not start.
description.blocked: The updater is running but cannot install updates right now.
description.busy: An update is announced or running.
description.demo: Installing updates is switched off in the public demo.

unavailable.title: The updater is not running
unavailable.body: Updates cannot be installed from this page until the updater runs. Choosing an update source under Settings only says where releases come from: it does not start the updater. Start it once on the server (see below), or update by hand with the commands below.

enable.title: Start the updater
enable.body: The updater is optional and is started once, on the server, in the folder that holds docker-compose.yml. Once it runs, this page can announce an update, take a database backup first, restart the services and roll back if the new version does not start. Nothing has to be changed in the .env file for it.
enable.socket: The updater mounts the Docker socket. That is root access to the host: whoever controls the updater controls this server. Start it only if you accept that.
enable.image: There is no separate updater image: the updater runs the application image ({image}) in another role. On its first start it pins that image in the .env file (RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE), and after every update from a signed release it moves itself to the new version.
enable.imageGeneric: There is no separate updater image: the updater runs the application image (RESTOW_IMAGE) in another role. On its first start it pins that image in the .env file (RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE), and after every update from a signed release it moves itself to the new version.

blocked.title: Updates are blocked
blocked.body: Nothing can be installed until this is fixed. Updating by hand still works.

blockers.docker_unreachable: The updater cannot reach Docker. Check that the Docker socket is mounted into the updater and that Docker is running.
blockers.compose_missing: The updater cannot find docker-compose.yml in the project folder. Use the docker-compose.yml of this release, or set RESTOW_PROJECT_DIR in the .env file to the absolute path of the folder that holds it, then recreate the updater.
blockers.project_dir_mismatch: The project folder the updater sees does not match the folder this installation runs from. Set RESTOW_PROJECT_DIR in the .env file to the absolute path of the folder that holds docker-compose.yml, then restart the updater.
blockers.env_unwritable: The updater cannot write the .env file. It has to write the new image reference there.
blockers.disk_space: There is not enough free disk space for a download and the database backup.
blockers.docker_cli_missing: The updater cannot find the Docker command line tool it needs to run Compose.
blockers.updater_image_unpinned: The updater takes its own image from RESTOW_IMAGE, the line it rewrites during an update, and could not pin it by itself. Set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE in the .env file to the application image (the same image as RESTOW_IMAGE; there is no separate updater image), or use the docker-compose.yml of this release, then recreate the updater.
blockers.unknown: The updater reported a problem this version does not know.

ready.body: Announce it with a lead time, so that everyone who is signed in can save their work.
ready.nothing: There is no newer release to install.

sourceNotAllowed.title: Building from this source is turned off
sourceNotAllowed.body: The updater builds from a custom repository only when the operator names it in the .env file on the server. Add this line to .env, then recreate the updater:
sourceNotAllowed.risk: What is built from that repository runs with full access to all backups and keys. Allow only a repository you trust as much as the release itself. Updating by hand keeps working.

incompatible.title: The updater must be recreated
incompatible.body: The updater is running but speaks an older protocol, so it is older than this installation. It runs the application image too: set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE in the .env file to the image in RESTOW_IMAGE (or rebuild restow:local when you build from source), recreate the updater and reload this page. From 0.2.1 on, the updater moves itself after each update. Until then, update by hand.

selfUpdate.pending: The updater is moving itself to version {version}, the image whose release signature it just verified. This takes a few seconds.
selfUpdate.failed: The update to {running} succeeded, but the updater could not move itself to it and still runs {updater}. {reason} The .env file already names the verified image; recreate the updater on the server, in the folder that holds docker-compose.yml:
selfUpdate.skipped: The updater runs version {updater} while this installation runs {running}. It did not move itself: {reason} Move it by hand: set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE in the .env file to the image in RESTOW_IMAGE (the updater runs the application image; there is no separate one), then recreate it:
selfUpdate.on: The updater runs version {updater} while this installation runs {running}, which was not installed by the updater. It moves itself after the next update it installs from a signed release. To move it now, set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE in the .env file to the image in RESTOW_IMAGE, then recreate it:
selfUpdate.legacy: The updater runs version {updater} while this installation runs {running}. This updater is older than the self-update and has to be moved once by hand: set RESTOW_UPDATER_IMAGE in the .env file to the image in RESTOW_IMAGE (the updater runs the application image; there is no separate one), then recreate it. From then on it follows every update by itself.

signaturesOff.body: Signature verification is switched off (RESTOW_UPDATER_VERIFY_SIGNATURES=false). What is installed is whatever lies under the published digest in the configured repository. For test installations only: switch it back on for production.

edition.title: Edition
edition.description: This installation runs the Community build: the Apache-2.0 core, without the Business and Service Provider modules.

adds.title: What the full build adds
adds.business: Business: the provider team (several administrators with roles), the archive's GoBD layer (journal receiver, enforced retention, legal hold), scheduled summary reports and the audit log viewer.
adds.serviceProvider: Service Provider: multiple tenants, team members limited to chosen tenants, the cross-tenant API and the provider dashboard.
adds.license: The full build runs as Community until a license key is installed, so switching changes nothing else by itself. Both builds use the same database.

edition.switched: The server already runs the full build. Reload this page to see the License section.

switch.title: Switch to the full build
switch.description: Moves this installation to the full images of the version it runs now.
switch.updater: The updater installs the full images of version {version}, checked against the release signature, after a database backup, and rolls back if they do not start.
switch.busy: An update is announced or running. Switch when it has finished.
switch.manual: Switch by hand on the server, in the folder that holds docker-compose.yml: set these two lines in the .env file, then pull the images and recreate the services.
switch.manualUnknown: Set RESTOW_IMAGE and RESTOW_WEB_IMAGE in the .env file to the full images (restow and restow-web) of the version this installation runs.
switch.enableUpdater: With the updater, this page does the switch for you. Start it once on the server: {command}
switch.oneWay: The switch goes one way only: the full build is not switched back to Community from here.
switch.announced: The switch to the full build is announced.

dialog.title: Switch to the full build?

dialog.updater: The updater moves to the full image as well, so later updates stay on the full build.
dialog.oneWay: There is no way back to the Community build from here.
